messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> P1: Rapid GPU queue growth in us-west1 (pool=inference-gpu-1). Auto-scaling failing. See incident console link <https://redwood.internal/incidents/2310001111>
Alice K: paging — multiple customers hitting 503/timeout, overall queue jumped from ~60 -> 380 in 6m :grimacing:
Bryan S (oncall): I'm up, joining a call now. Any immediate mitigations?
Samir R: autoscaler logs show repeated scaleUp attempts rejected with error: \"quotaExceeded: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED\" for GPU quota in project redwood-prod-usw1
Maria D: Confirmed with cloud-ops: project-level GPU quota in us-west1 is at hard cap. No available GPUs to allocate.
cloud-ops: Opening emergency case with GCP support, requesting temporary quota bump. Case CJ-98765 created. ETA initial response ~12m.
Beth L: Impact assessment: ~12% of hosted API requests failing, total RPS down ~25% last 10m. Enterprise customers with reserved capacity mostly OK.
Alice K: Short-term mitigations we can apply: 1) route non-enterprise traffic to eu-west1, 2) enable model fallback to smaller quantized variant, 3) aggressive prefix caching to reduce tokens.
Bryan S (oncall): I'll push a region-pref routing rule for non-enterprise keys now. Running:
```
redwoodctl routes set --region-preference eu-west1 --filter 'tier!=enterprise'
```
Samir R: Also applying model fallback on affected pools: rw-large -> rw-medium-quant to reduce memory per replica. Doing gradual rollback if errors spike.
Maria D: Note: autoscaler tries to request new instances but GCP returns 403/QUOTA_DENIED on instance create with GPUs. We need account owner approval for cross-project quota emergency or GCP to raise limit.
Alice K: Estimated customer-impact window if no quota change: 40-60m. If GCP approves bump faster we can recover quicker.
incident-bot: On-call handoff scheduled in 30m to Bryan S (oncall).
Bryan S (oncall): Acknowledged. Adding runbook steps to thread. Escalating to Sales Ops if SLA breaches >10% for any paying customer.
cloud-ops: GCP replied: temporary +50 GPU quota approved for 2 hours, will apply in ~16m. Monitoring the apply now.
Beth L: While we wait I disabled non-critical batch prewrites and rebalanced some jobs to free up ~8 GPU equivalents. Also enabled more aggressive KV prefix caching.
Samir R: After these mitigations queue dropped to ~120, p95 latency for routed requests improved from 1.4s -> 480ms. Error rate down from 12% -> 4% for routed traffic.
Maria D: Cost note: temporary capacity +50 GPUs estimated incremental cost ~$2.3k for the window, finance notified.
Alice K: Post-incident action items taking notes: alert for GPU headroom, autoscaler preflight to proactively request quota, runbook update to include immediate routing rule, and a test for model-fallback safety.
Bryan S (oncall): If the quota bump is delayed beyond 30m plan B is to spin up dedicated hosts in aws-us-west2 with spare credits and failover routing. cloud-ops please prepare AMI and terraform patch.
deploy-bot: Canary config applied: region-pref rule active for 15% of non-enterprise traffic.
Samir R: FYI support — I DM'd Support Ops about workaround steps for customer X who reported degraded image-gen jobs. They provided guidance to retry with lower context size.
Beth L: Updating status page and incident channel to reflect partial mitigation and recovery in-progress :white_check_mark:.
Alice K: Leaving a short checklist for postmortem:
- timeline and root cause: project-level GPU quota exhaustion in us-west1 combined with autoscaler boundary conditions prevented scale-up
- short-term remediation: emergency quota bump, regional routing, model fallback, cache/freeing of resources
- action items: add headroom alerts, implement autoscaler quota preflight, test runbook actions quarterly, update account escalation path with cloud vendor
Bryan S (oncall): Handing off to Maria D in 35m. I'll stay on the call until traffic normalizes. If anything urgent ping @pagerduty.
Maria D: Acknowledged, will takeover at 2310001400. Will coordinate postmortem and customer comms.
